messages.subject_clean: Proposal: a new binary package, r-pkg-team-core-architecture
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I would like to go ahead with this proposal and opened a MR on dh-r at:

https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/dh-r/-/merge_requests/20

Here are some extra answers to Dirk (taking into account the later
exchange with Rebecca).

Le Mon, Jun 22, 2026 at 07:09:33AM -0500, Dirk Eddelbuettel a écrit :
> Would you be able to demonstrate for R and, say, a handful of packages that
> there is fundaemtal "brokenness"?  And if you were to find it at the R level,
> would it not your normal "Good Open Source Citizen" responsibility to
> document this at the upstream bug tracker?  For R, that is its bugzilla; for
> packages often their GH repos. Can we not start there?  That would also be a
> net benefit to the R Project which AFAIK has no access to armhf s390x and
> likely also little to none for i386.

Sadly, yes, there is one problematic architecture, and it slipped out
of the restriction that we went through in the past 6 months: riscv64.

I am tracking the current issues on our wiki:

https://wiki.debian.org/R/riscv64/DebianIssues

I think that it is the tip of the iceberg, and that the main reason why
bugs are hitting particularly high-profile packages is that their test
coverage is better.

The core issue is the same in all cases and explained here, as we
discussed earlier.

https://wiki.debian.org/R/riscv64

I asked three times the riscv64 porters on their mailing list to give me
comments on this wiki page, explained that even just a "LGTM" would be
fine, but got no answer.  While I wrote earlier that I would contact the
R developers as well, I am wondering if it is going to be fruitful if
nobody is expressing interest on the Debian side.  I will expand on this
in a separate email, maybe next week.

This said, what I did on risvc64 illustrates what I would like to ask to
the people interested in the architecures where we do not build the
packages at the moment (like the two developpers from IBM and Canonical
who enquired about s390x).  I think that it is fair to say that we (the
people working or R packages in Debian) should not be alone in charge of
the whole process.

> I think our choice of 'mixing' package versions when CRAN is more or less
> ensuring a buildable cohort 'at HEAD' at each point in time is still the more
> likely issue.

Well, it is not a choice.  For most of the team-maintained packages that
are out of date today, the reason is either 1) we need to package new
dependencies, 2) there are new test failures on amd64 and I will not
upload until they are resolved, or 3) potential license issues such as
"must not modify" statements (in UK open government data for instance)
or "non-commercial" statements (and third-party upstream authors can not
be reached anymore).  Nothing that we can not solve in the long term,
but enough to create a backlog.

> [1] https://rousseeuwprize.org/2026

That is a really great news, thanks for the information!

Cheers,

Charles

> --
> dirk.eddelbuettel.com | @eddelbuettel | edd at debian.org

--

| Le Mon, Jun 22, 2026 at 07:09:33AM -0500, Dirk Eddelbuettel a écrit :
| >I think our choice of 'mixing' package versions when CRAN is more or less
| >ensuring a buildable cohort 'at HEAD' at each point in time is still the more
| >likely issue.
| 
| Well, it is not a choice.  For most of the team-maintained packages that

Everything we do is a choice.

Let me be more blunt if the subtler language does not work:

 - this team is very ambitious and adds encompassing autopkgtests spanning
   hardware platforms that CRAN does not run on

 - this team has generally speaking difficulties keeping up with CRAN and is
   therefore slipping behind releases at CRAN.

This creates a combinations where we end up testing BOTH on more platforms
AND ALSO on random package combinations CRAN does not test.

The combination is bound to set us up for failure and a lot of work. I think
something has got to give. I would limit autopkgtests to amd64 for a start,
until we are in alignment with CRAN and pass (ideally) everywhere. Then add
one architecture at a time. 

That said, I do appreciate the added color on that risk platform. There can
be / are always some platform that drift too far away. E.g. "eventually"
Debian turned m68k off as a release arch. We may well be at a point where we
decide similarly for R packages and some archirecture. And I am not against
that. But I wonder if were to do that, should we not also do it at the R
engine level, i.e. package r-base-core, and then ask for all 500-some binary
packages on that platform?

Dirk

-- 
dirk.eddelbuettel.com | @eddelbuettel | edd at debian.org

messages.subject: uscan V5 Templates for CRAN and Bioconductor ready for use.
messages.subject_clean: uscan V5 Templates for CRAN and Bioconductor ready for use.
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

in the past months I have worked on uscan V5 templates for CRAN and
Bioconductor.  With devscripts version 2.26.9 now backported for stable
and installed on the relevant parts Debian infrastructure, the templates
are ready for use in our packages.

For CRAN package, old watch files can be replaced by:

```
Version: 5

Template: CRAN
Name: the_upstream_name
```

For Bioconductor, the name of the template is… Bioconductor.

Both templates honor the `Files-excluded` field of `debian/copyright` if
present, and will use the +dfsg prefix to indicate that the package has
been repackaged.  Thus they are a replacement for both repackaged and
unchanged upstream sources.

https://salsa.debian.org/debian/devscripts/-/tree/main/lib/Devscripts/Uscan/Templates

There is even more: if the package has an `Archive` field in
`d/upstream/metadata` and an `Upstream-Name` field in `d/copyright` the
`d/watch` file can be deleted entirely.  But a bunch of quality control
tools still see this as a defect, so I do not recommend it yet.

I hope you will enjoy the templates, and have a nice Sunday!

Charles

--

messages.subject: Ready for Bioconductor transition?
messages.body_plain:
Good morning everybody!

Now that the architecture restriction mass upload is behind us, that most
issues with testing migration appear to be either riscv64 or reproducibility
regressions, and now that we can express architecture support with our brand
new r-pkg-team-core-architecture metapackage, I would like to propose to go
ahead with the much awaited Bioconductor transition.

In the past, one of the major headaches was that if a new dependency would be
found by surprise at the middle of the transition, it could delay the process
by weeks or even months.  Now, thanks to the pereverance of Andreas during his
DPL terms, the waiting time in the NEW queue can be less than a day.

So one thing that we could to is to get the green light of the Release team
and just go for the transition sequentially.

Please let me know if you see some issues with the simplest plan, your
availability, collisions with other transitions, etc.

Have a nice day,

Charles

--
